cards.title: Site + API deploy on push to main
cards.brief:
Push to main deploys the static site (hackathon.tyneside.software) and the API. A normal change does not need a manual Cloud Run click or a Pages republish.

Done when

  • A push to site main updates the live GitHub Pages site.
  • A push to API main updates the live health endpoint.
  • Local .\start.ps1 still works for development.

cards.title: Cloud Run API live + CORS for Pages
cards.brief:
Deploy hackathon-api to Cloud Run in London (europe-west2), allow unauthenticated /health, and CORS for GitHub Pages plus local :5500. Paste the service URL into config.js as window.HACKATHON_API.

Done when

  • Public Cloud Run URL serves /health.
  • The site on Pages (and localhost:5500) can call it without a CORS error.
  • Local uvicorn still works; Cloud Run is extra, not a replacement for the first hours.

Blocked on

  • Michael back / GCP project access. Do not burn the first two hours on this.

How

  1. Dockerfile and FastAPI scaffold are already in the API repo.
  2. gcloud run deploy hackathon-api --source . --region europe-west2 --allow-unauthenticated with CORS_ORIGINS set.
  3. Point hackathon-site/config.js at the service URL. Include that file from the pages that will call the API.

cards.title: Lewis: get the front end running locally
cards.brief:
Clone the org site repo and prove Home, Map, and Board load on your machine. Do not open HTML as file:// — the browser will block the API later.

Done when

  • http://127.0.0.1:5500/ serves the desktop home.
  • Map and Board open from the nav without a blank page.

How

  1. Clone Tyneside-Software/hackathon-site next to hackathon-api.
  2. From the site folder run .\start.ps1 (site + API) or python -m http.server 5500 (site only). serve.ps1 was removed.
  3. Click through Home, Map, Board.
Onboarding steps

cards.title: Reeve: get the back end running locally
cards.brief:
Local FastAPI on :8080. Reeve already scaffolded the health route; this card is “it runs on my machine”, not “write the API”.

Done when

  • http://127.0.0.1:8080/health returns JSON with ok: true.
  • /docs is reachable.

How

  1. Clone hackathon-api next to the site.
  2. Create .venv, install requirements.txt, run uvicorn on 8080 — or use .\start.ps1.
Onboarding steps

cards.title: Lewis: get the back end running locally
cards.brief:
Clone the API as a sibling of the site and get FastAPI answering on port 8080. This is the health-check loop, not Cloud Run.

Done when

  • GET http://127.0.0.1:8080/health returns ok.
  • /docs loads the Swagger UI.

How

  1. Clone Tyneside-Software/hackathon-api next to the site.
  2. python -m venv .venv then pip install -r requirements.txt.
  3. uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8080 (or just .\start.ps1 from the site folder).
Onboarding steps

cards.title: Lewis: GitHub edit → run → push (site repo)
cards.brief:
Prove the org-repo loop on hackathon-site: a tiny visible change, still runs, then push to origin/main. Not a personal fork unless you have been told otherwise.

Done when

  • Your commit is on Tyneside-Software/hackathon-site.
  • Home / Map / Board still load after the change.
  • This card moves to Done.

How

  1. Pull latest main.
  2. Make a small visible edit (name in a comment, README line, harmless label).
  3. Confirm it still runs locally.
  4. git add · git commit · git push origin main.
Git steps

cards.title: Reeve: GitHub edit → run → push (API repo)
cards.brief:
Prove the org-repo loop on hackathon-api. Tiny change, still serves /health, then push to origin/main.

Done when

  • Commit is visible on Tyneside-Software/hackathon-api.
  • /health still works after the change.

How

  1. Pull latest, edit something harmless (comment, README, label).
  2. Hit /health again.
  3. git add · git commit · git push origin main.
Git steps

cards.title: Reeve: start script for front end and back end together
cards.brief:
start.ps1 already lives in the site repo. This card is: a teammate can clone both repos as siblings, run one command, and get site :5500 plus API :8080 without asking anyone.

Done when

  • From hackathon-site, .\start.ps1 opens two windows.
  • Site and /health both work. If the venv is missing, the script creates it.
  • A teammate who is not Reeve can follow the README and succeed.

How

  1. Keep site and API as sibling folders.
  2. Fix the script if paths, quoting, or venv creation fail on a clean machine.
  3. Document the command in the README (already started).
cards.tag: one command, two processes, no asking the AI

cards.title: Save routes in the browser (localStorage)
cards.brief:
Persist the current waypoint list in the browser so a refresh does not wipe a demo. No API. This is the persistence story until card 11.

Done when

  • Add stops, refresh, they come back on the map and in the sidebar.
  • Clear still clears, including storage.
  • Home / Board still load if storage is empty or corrupt — never a blank map.

How

  1. Write waypoints (lat/lng order) to localStorage from app/map.js.
  2. Restore on load, then let the user Calculate route as today.
  3. Do not block on Cloud Run.
Open map

cards.title: Job list beside the map (seed Howden-shaped jobs)
cards.brief:
A job list in the map sidebar, seeded with Howden-shaped work: named jobs, rough Tyneside locations. This is the first hint of dispatch, not a full scheduler.

Done when

  • At least five seed jobs visible beside the map without an API.
  • Clicking a job does something visible (focus the map, highlight, or drop its waypoint).
  • The existing waypoint + route flow still works if you ignore the list.

How

  1. Hard-code a small JSON/JS list in the map page (name, area, lat/lng).
  2. Render it in the existing sidebar; keep the layout usable on a laptop.
  3. Shape the names like real cleaning/logistics jobs, not “Test 1”.
Open map

cards.title: Demo seed: 5 Tyneside waypoints + named run
cards.brief:
One-click demo so nobody has to click the map five times during a show-and-tell. Load a named run with five Tyneside waypoints already placed.

Done when

  • A button (e.g. “Load Tyneside demo”) drops five named stops and a run name.
  • Calculate route works immediately on that seed.
  • Clear still returns to an empty map.

How

  1. Pick five real-ish spots around Newcastle / Tyneside (not a straight line down one street).
  2. Give the run a name the operator can see in the sidebar.
  3. Keep the manual click-to-add path working.
Open map

cards.title: Local “who am I” account (name in the browser)
cards.brief:
No real auth. A display name stored in the browser so the chrome can say who is driving the demo. Later job assignment can reuse it.

Done when

  • You can set a name from the site (prompt, form, or nav control).
  • It survives refresh.
  • It is visible in the chrome (nav or map sidebar). Empty name is a valid empty state, not a crash.

How

  1. localStorage for the name. Keep it off the API until card 10.
  2. Show it on more than one page if the chrome is shared; otherwise map + home is enough.

cards.title: Persist routes on the API (replace localStorage)
cards.brief:
Replace browser-only route storage with API persistence so two machines can share a run. Card 06 stays as the fallback if the API is down — the map must not go blank.

Done when

  • POST (or PUT) a route, GET it back from the Cloud Run URL.
  • Save on one browser, load on another.
  • If the API errors, localStorage or a visible error keeps the page usable.

Blocked on

  • Card 10 (live API + CORS).

How

  1. Minimal routes resource: id, name, waypoints, maybe duration/distance.
  2. In-memory is acceptable for the hackathon if two requests to the same instance work; say so in the brief if it is not durable.
  3. Wire the map save/load to window.HACKATHON_API.

cards.title: Map with clickable / draggable waypoints
cards.brief:
Leaflet map centred on Newcastle. Click to drop a stop, drag to move it, remove from the list. This is the visual spine of the night: dispatch starts with a map that never looks dead.

Done when

  • Someone else can add two pins without a briefing.
  • Drag updates the sidebar coordinates.
  • Clear removes pins and the route line.

What’s live

  • app/index.html + app/map.js — OSM tiles, draggable markers, stop list with remove.
Open map →

cards.title: Route calculation between waypoints
cards.brief:
Calculate a driving route through the waypoints. Public OSRM when the network is up; haversine straight-line fallback if it fails, so the board never looks broken.

Done when

  • Two or more stops + Calculate route draws a line.
  • Sidebar shows distance, time, and engine (OSRM driving or straight-line).
  • OSRM down still produces a visible line, not an empty map.

What’s live

  • https://router.project-osrm.org for the driving geometry.
  • Fallback assumes ~35 km/h for a rough time estimate.
Open map →

What’s live
